body.statement: Every cell of \(\mathfrak W_\delta(a)\) fixes the full midrank vector, every value \(T(z,b)\), and every indicator in \(p(a,b)\). Hence \(P_\delta(a)\) is a maximum over the finite complete weak-order complex, equality faces included, and is attained. If the observed outcomes are rational, every nonempty cell has a rational representative of polynomial encoding length.
body.justification: This theorem converts an unbounded missing-outcome optimization into a finite exact object without discarding ties.
body.gap: Li, Sheng, and Yu obtain an extreme-completion closed form from an exchangeable assignment law together with an altered deterministic unit-index tie-breaking convention. Ordinary midranks under arbitrary explicitly listed rational assignment weights instead require the equality-inclusive chamber maximum.
body.consumer: It supplies a checkable finite certificate for exact attrition-robust testing under rerandomization and other restricted designs.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(a\), \(\delta\), and a completion \(b\in\mathcal C_\delta(a)\).  The relation
\[
i\preceq_b j\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad b_i\le b_j
\]
is a total preorder on the finite set \(I\).  Its equivalence classes are the equality blocks of \(b\), ordered by their common values.  Conversely, the definition of \(\mathfrak W_\delta(a)\) retains exactly those ordered partitions that extend the fixed ordered partition of the observed coordinates.

Consider a block \(D\) of cardinality \(d\) having exactly \(c\) labels in earlier blocks.  By the definition of the midrank, every \(i\in D\) has
\[
r_i(b)=1+c+\frac{d-1}{2}=c+\frac{d+1}{2}.
\]
Thus a cell of \(\mathfrak W_\delta(a)\) fixes every coordinate of \(r(b)\).  It consequently fixes \(T(z,b)=\sum_i z_i r_i(b)\) for each \(z\in\Omega\), fixes each comparison \(T(z,b)\ge T(a,b)\), and, by the midrank-tail definition, fixes \(p(a,b)\).

There are only finitely many total preorders on the finite set \(I\).  By the definition of \(\mathfrak W_\delta(a)\), each of its cells is nonempty.  Therefore the finite set of values of \(p(a,b)\) over these cells has a largest element.  Every completion induces one of the cells, while each cell has a realizing completion, so the robust-p-value definition gives
\[
P_\delta(a)
=\max_{\preceq\in\mathfrak W_\delta(a)}
  \sum_{z\in\Omega}w_z
  \mathbf 1\{T(z,\preceq)\ge T(a,\preceq)\}.
\]
In particular, the supremum is attained.  This argument includes equality blocks; no continuity or compactness assertion is being used.

It remains to establish the encoding claim.  Suppose the distinct observed coordinates are rational numbers \(c_1<\cdots<c_g\).  For a compatible cell, attach every missing label that shares an observed block to its prescribed \(c_j\).  If a gap \((c_j,c_{j+1})\) contains \(q\) missing-only blocks, assign them, in order, the values
\[
c_j+\frac{u}{q+1}(c_{j+1}-c_j),\qquad u=1,\ldots,q.
\]
Assign consecutive integer translates below \(c_1\) and above \(c_g\) to exterior missing-only blocks.  If \(g=0\), assign consecutive integers to all blocks.  These choices realize precisely the prescribed strict and equality relations.  Each new denominator has binary length bounded by the total input length plus \(O(\log(k+1))\), and the same is true after the indicated rational additions and multiplications.  Hence the whole representative has polynomial encoding length.  This proves every assertion.
